title: Derived Hom from a semidualizing complex detects bounded coherent isomorphisms
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Work in its ordinary module derived category $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with $R\operatorname{Hom}$ as the internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-object ringed site. Write $D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(A)$ for objects with bounded, finitely generated cohomology. Let $C\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(A)$ and assume the scalar-action morphism $A\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,C)$ is an isomorphism. For every $Z\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(A)$, the equality $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,Z)=0$ implies $Z=0$. Consequently, for any morphism $f:X\to Y$ with $X,Y\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(A)$, if $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,f)$ is an isomorphism then $f$ is an isomorphism. No finite projective or injective dimension of $C$ is assumed.

source.place: Agent corollary of Tag 0BFR (complete Noetherian local rings have dualizing complexes) and Tag 0A7C (duality on coherent complexes, including unbounded coherent complexes), using more-algebra.tex Tags 0A6A (flat RHom base change), 0A65 (tensor-Hom adjunction), and derived Nakayama. Proof of the corollary is explained in report.md; it is not asserted to be the statement of Tag 0A7C.

proof.text: First record how the hypotheses pass through a flat map $A\to B$ with $B$ Noetherian. Exactness of tensor [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], applied to the cycle, boundary and cohomology exact sequences of a representative complex, gives $H^i(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B)=H^i(K)\otimes_A B$: termwise tensor preserves acyclic complexes, so computes its derived functor. A finite generating family tensored with $1$ still generates. Hence $C_B,Z_B$ have bounded finite cohomology. The Noetherian pseudo-coherence criterion applies to $C$. The flat RHom comparison, with $E=C$ and respectively $L=Z,C$, therefore gives $R\operatorname{Hom}_B(C_B,Z_B)=0$ and an isomorphism $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,C)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_B(C_B,C_B)$. Both targets $Z,C$ are bounded below as required.

source.place: Agent flat-reduction argument; more-algebra.tex Tag 0A6A, case (3).

proof.text: The latter comparison carries the scalar-action morphism to scalar action on $C_B$. To check the actual map, choose a bounded-above finite free model $P$ of $C$ using the pseudo-coherence criterion. The projective Hom model [lem-pod-projective-hom-evaluation-model] represents its derived endomorphisms by $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_A(P,P)$. Scalar action sends $a$ to the chain endomorphism $p\mapsto ap$. By the stated construction of flat RHom comparison, after scalar extension this map is sent to the endomorphism $p\otimes b\mapsto ap\otimes b$. Extending $B$-linearly gives exactly $p\otimes b\mapsto p\otimes sb$ for a scalar $s\in B$. Since $P\otimes_A B$ models $C_B$, this is its scalar-action map $B\to R\operatorname{Hom}_B(C_B,C_B)$. Thus the scalar-action isomorphism persists under the flat change of rings.

source.place: Agent chain-model verification of homothety compatibility for the canonical map of more-algebra.tex Tag 0A6A.

proof.text: Now suppose $(A,\mathfrak m)$ itself is complete local. Choose $\Omega$ from coherent duality [lem-trf-complete-local-coherent-duality], and set $W=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(Z,\Omega)$. The bounded clause gives $W\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(A)$, and canonical biduality gives $Z\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_A(W,\Omega)$. The tensor lemma gives $T=C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}W\in D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(A)$. In particular $T$ is in the unbounded coherent category on which this duality applies; no lower bound on its cohomology has been asserted.

source.place: Agent reduction to coherent duality: Tags 0BFR and 0A7C; tensor closure from more-algebra.tex Tag 0DJE.

proof.text: On the one-object ringed site, tensor-Hom adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] identifies $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(T,\Omega)$ with $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,R\operatorname{Hom}_A(W,\Omega))\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,Z)=0$. Biduality for $T\in D_{\mathrm{fg}}(A)$ gives $T\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_A(0,\Omega)=0$. A local ring with a maximal ideal is nonzero. If $C=0$, its derived endomorphism object is zero, contradicting the homothety isomorphism $A\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,C)$. Hence $C\ne0$. Tensor nonvanishing then gives $W=0$, and biduality for $Z$ gives $Z\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_A(0,\Omega)=0$. This proves the complete-local case.

source.place: Agent complete-local argument using Tag 0A7C on all coherent complexes and more-algebra.tex Tag 0A65.

proof.text: For an arbitrary Noetherian local ring $(A,\mathfrak m)$ form $\widehat A=\varprojlim A/\mathfrak m^n$. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] and local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\widehat A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring]. Since the Noetherian ideal $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated, [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] says $\widehat A$ is complete for that maximal ideal. The map $A\to\widehat A$ is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat]. Steps 1--2 transport both hypotheses and both bounded-coherent objects to $\widehat A$, so steps 3--4 give $Z\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}\widehat A=0$.

source.place: Agent faithfully-flat completion reduction preceding application of Tag 0BFR.

proof.text: By the cycle calculation of step 1, $H^i(Z)\otimes_A\widehat A=0$ for every $i$. Faithfully flat tensor detection [lem-sc-faithfully-flat-tensor-zero] implies $H^i(Z)=0$ for all $i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] to $Z\to0$ to conclude $Z=0$. This proves the assertion for every Noetherian local ring.

source.place: Agent descent of zero cohomology along the faithfully flat completion.

proof.text: For a general $A$ and every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, the localization $A_{\mathfrak m}$ is flat over $A$ and Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. It is local: a fraction with numerator outside $\mathfrak m$ is a unit, and all other fractions form the proper ideal $\mathfrak mA_{\mathfrak m}$. Steps 1--2 transport the hypotheses, and the local result gives $Z\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A_{\mathfrak m}=0$. The same flat cohomology calculation says $H^i(Z)_{\mathfrak m}=0$. For each $i$ apply [lem-weil-pbc-linear-map-bijective-at-maximal-localizations] to $H^i(Z)\to0$: all its maximal localizations are bijective, so $H^i(Z)=0$. The cohomological isomorphism criterion gives $Z=0$. This also covers the zero ring, since the cited maximal-localization criterion allows an empty set of maximal ideals.

Finally let $f:X\to Y$ be as in the statement and choose its distinguished cone triangle $X\to Y\to T\to X[1]$ in the ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] gives short exact sequences $0\to\operatorname{coker}H^i(f)\to H^i(T)\to\ker H^{i+1}(f)\to0$. The kernel is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]; the cokernel is generated by the images of generators of $H^i(Y)$. Lift generators of the kernel to $H^i(T)$ and adjoin generators of the cokernel to obtain a finite generating set. The same sequence makes $H^i(T)$ zero outside a finite interval. Thus $T\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(A)$.

source.place: Agent cone argument; derived-category cohomology exactness.

proof.text: Exactness in the second variable of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] sends the cone triangle to a distinguished triangle whose first arrow is $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,f)$. Since that arrow is an isomorphism, [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] gives $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,T)=0$. The object-detection result just proved applies to this bounded-coherent $T$, hence $T=0$. Applying the same cone criterion to the original triangle gives that $f$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Agent conclusion by exactness of derived Hom and the zero-cone criterion.
